cues.en: What I am going to show you are the astonishing molecular machines that create the living
cues.zh: 我要向大家展示的，是构建出你身体生命

cues.en: fabric of your body.
cues.zh: 结构的惊人分子机器。

cues.en: Now molecules are really, really tiny and by tiny I mean really.
cues.zh: 分子其实非常、非常微小，我说的微小是真的极小。

cues.en: They're smaller than the wavelength of light so we have no way to directly observe them
cues.zh: 它们比光的波长还要小，所以我们无法直接观测到它们，

cues.en: but through science we do have a fairly good idea of what's going on down at the molecular
cues.zh: 但借助科学，我们对分子层面的运作

cues.en: scale.
cues.zh: 已经有了相当清楚的了解。

cues.en: So what we can do is actually tell you about the molecules but we don't really have a direct way of showing you the molecules.
cues.zh: 因此，我们能向你描述这些分子，却无法直接将它们展现给你看。

cues.en: One way around this is to draw pictures and this idea is actually nothing new.
cues.zh: 解决这个问题的一个办法是画图，而这种想法其实并不新鲜。

cues.en: Scientists have always created pictures as part of their thinking and discovery process.
cues.zh: 科学家一直都把画图当作思考和探索过程的一部分。

cues.en: They draw pictures of what they're observing with their eyes through technology like telescopes and microscopes,
cues.zh: 他们画下通过望远镜和显微镜等技术亲眼所见的内容，

cues.en: and also what they're thinking about in their minds.
cues.zh: 也画下脑海中思考的景象。

cues.en: I picked two well-known examples because they're very well known for expressing science through art and I start with Galileo
cues.zh: 我选了两个著名的例子，因为他们都以通过艺术表达科学而闻名，首先是伽利略

cues.en: who used the world's first telescope to look at the moon and he
cues.zh: 他用世界上第一架望远镜观察月球，并且

cues.en: Transformed our understanding of the moon the perception of the 17th century was the moon was a perfect heavenly sphere
cues.zh: 彻底颠覆了我们对月球的认知，17世纪时人们还认为月球是一个完美的神圣天体

cues.en: but what Galileo saw was a rocky barren world which he expressed through his watercolor painting a
cues.zh: 但伽利略看到的却是一个布满岩石的荒凉世界，他通过自己的水彩画表现了出来

cues.en: A, another scientist with very big ideas, the superstar of biology is Charles Darwin.
cues.zh: 另一位有着极其伟大构想的科学家，生物学界的巨星，是查尔斯·达尔文。

cues.en: And with this famous entry in his notebook, he begins in the top left-hand corner with,
cues.zh: 在他笔记本上这则著名的记录里，他从左上角以这几个字开始：

cues.en: I think, and then sketches out the first tree of life, which is his perception of how
cues.zh: “我想”，然后勾勒出了第一张生命之树的草图，表达了他对于

cues.en: all the species, all living things on Earth are connected through evolutionary history,
cues.zh: 地球上所有物种、所有生物如何通过进化历史相互联系的理解，

cues.en: the origin of species through natural selection and divergence from an ancestral population.
cues.zh: 即通过自然选择以及从祖先种群的分化而形成的物种起源。

cues.en: Even as a scientist, I used to go to lectures by molecular biologists and find them completely incomprehensible
cues.zh: 即使作为一名科学家，我过去去听分子生物学家的讲座时，也觉得完全听不懂

cues.en: with all the fancy technical language and jargon that they would use in describing their work
cues.zh: 因为他们在描述自己的工作时，用了大量花哨的技术语言和专业行话

cues.en: until I encountered the artworks of David Goodsell, who was a molecular biologist at the Scripps Institute
cues.zh: 直到我看到了 David Goodsell 的艺术作品，他是斯克利普斯研究所的一位分子生物学家

cues.en: and his pictures are all, everything's accurate, it's all to scale
cues.zh: 他的画作非常严谨，全都是按比例精确绘制的

cues.en: and his work illuminated for me what the molecular world inside us is like
cues.zh: 他的作品为我展现了我们体内的分子世界究竟是什么模样

cues.en: So, this is a transection through blood.
cues.zh: 这是一张血液的横截面图。

cues.en: In the top left-hand corner, you've got this yellow-green area.
cues.zh: 在左上角，你能看到这一片黄绿色的区域。

cues.en: The yellow-green area is the fluids of blood, which is mostly water, but it's also antibodies,
cues.zh: 黄绿色区域是血浆，大部分是水，但也包含抗体、

cues.en: sugars, hormones, that kind of thing.
cues.zh: 糖分、激素这类的物质。

cues.en: And the red region is a slice into a red blood cell, and those red molecules are hemoglobin.
cues.zh: 红色的区域则是红细胞的切面，那些红色的分子就是血红蛋白。

cues.en: They are actually red.
cues.zh: 它们实际上是红色的。

cues.en: That's what gives blood its color.
cues.zh: 血液的颜色就是由此而来的。

cues.en: And hemoglobin acts as a molecular sponge to soak up the oxygen in your lungs and then
cues.zh: 血红蛋白就像一个分子海绵，吸收肺部的氧气，

cues.en: carry it to other parts of the body.
cues.zh: 然后输送到身体的其他部位。

cues.en: I was very much inspired by this image many years ago, and I wondered whether we
cues.zh: 很多年前，这幅图像给了我极大的启发，我当时在想，

cues.en: could use computer graphics to represent the molecular world.
cues.zh: 我们能否用计算机图形来呈现分子世界？

cues.en: What would it look like?
cues.zh: 它会是什么样子的？

cues.en: And that's how I really began.
cues.zh: 我就这样开始了探索。

cues.en: So let's begin.
cues.zh: 现在让我们开始吧。

cues.en: This is DNA, and it's classic double helix form.
cues.zh: 这就是 DNA，呈经典的双螺旋结构。

cues.en: And it's from x-ray crystallography,
cues.zh: 它是通过 X 射线晶体学获得的，

cues.en: so it's an accurate model of DNA.
cues.zh: 所以是一个精确的 DNA 模型。

cues.en: If we unwind the double helix and unzip the two strands,
cues.zh: 如果我们解开双螺旋，把两条链分开，

cues.en: you see these things that look like teeth.
cues.zh: 就会看到这些像牙齿一样的东西。

cues.en: Those are the letters of genetic code, the 25,000 genes
cues.zh: 这些就是遗传密码的字母，写在你 DNA 里的

cues.en: you've got written in your DNA.
cues.zh: 那两万五千个基因。

cues.en: This is what they typically talk about, the genetic code.
cues.zh: 这就是人们通常所说的遗传密码。

cues.en: This is what they're talking about.
cues.zh: 这就是他们所谈论的。

cues.en: But I want to talk about a different aspect of DNA
cues.zh: 但我想谈谈DNA科学的另一个方面，

cues.en: science, and that is the physical nature of DNA, and it's these two strands that run in
cues.zh: 也就是DNA的物理特性，正是这两条反向平行的链，

cues.en: opposite directions for reasons I can't go into right now, but they physically run in
cues.zh: 出于某些我现在无法细说的原因，它们在物理上呈反向走向，

cues.en: opposite directions, which creates a number of complications for your living cells as
cues.zh: 正如你即将看到的，这给活细胞带来了许多复杂的问题，

cues.en: you're about to see, most particularly when DNA is being copied.
cues.zh: 尤其是在DNA进行复制的时候。

cues.en: And so what I'm about to show you is an accurate representation of the actual DNA replication
cues.zh: 因此，我即将向你们展示的，正是此刻正在你体内运转的

cues.en: machine that's occurring right now inside your body, at least 2002 biology.
cues.zh: 真实DNA复制机器的精确重现，至少基于2002年的生物学研究。

cues.en: So DNA is entering the production line from the left-hand side, and it hits this collection,
cues.zh: DNA正从左侧进入这条“生产线”，遇到这组装配，

cues.en: this miniature biochemical machines that are pulling apart the DNA strand and making an
cues.zh: 这些微型生化机器将DNA双链拆开，并制作出

cues.en: exact copy.
cues.zh: 完全相同的副本。

cues.en: So DNA comes in, it hits this blue donut-shaped structure, and it's ripped apart into its
cues.zh: DNA 进入后，撞上这个蓝色的环状结构，被撕开成了

cues.en: two strands.
cues.zh: 两条链。

cues.en: One strand can be copied directly, and it can be seen spooling off down to the bottom
cues.zh: 其中一条可以直接复制，能看到它一直延伸到了底端，

cues.en: there, but things aren't so simple as the other strand because it must be copied backwards.
cues.zh: 但另一条链就没那么简单了，因为它必须反向复制。

cues.en: So it's thrown out repeatedly in these loops and copied one section at a time, creating
cues.zh: 所以它会反复甩出这样的环圈，一次复制一段，最终生成

cues.en: two new DNA molecules. Now, you have billions of this machine right now whirring the right
cues.zh: 两个新的 DNA 分子。现在，你体内正有数十亿台这样的机器在运转，

cues.en: way inside you, copying your DNA with exquisite fidelity. It's an accurate representation
cues.zh: 以极高的保真度复制着你的 DNA。这是一个精确的模型，

cues.en: and it's pretty much at the correct speed for what's occurring inside you. But I've
cues.zh: 其速度也基本还原了你体内真实发生的情况。但我省略了

cues.en: left out error correction and a bunch of other things. This was work from a number
cues.zh: 错误修正和许多其他机制。这是几年前的

cues.en: of years ago. Thank you. This is work from a number of years ago. But I want to show
cues.zh: 研究成果了。谢谢大家。这是几年前的工作了。接下来我想给

cues.en: you next is updated science. It's updated technology. So again, we begin with DNA, and
cues.zh: 大家看的是最新的科学进展，是最新的技术。所以我们依然从 DNA 开始，

cues.en: it's jiggling and wiggling there because of the surrounding soup of molecules which
cues.zh: 它在那里不断抖动晃动，是因为周围充斥着大量分子，

cues.en: are stripped away so you can see something. DNA is about 2 nanometers across, which is
cues.zh: 为了让大家看清楚，我们把这些分子去掉了。DNA 的直径大约只有 2 纳米，

cues.en: really quite tiny. But in each one of your cells, each strand of DNA is about 30 to
cues.zh: 真的非常微小。但在你的每一个细胞里，每条 DNA 链大约有

cues.en: 40 million nanometers long.
cues.zh: 三四千万纳米长。

cues.en: So, to keep the DNA organized, to regulate access to the genetic code, it's wrapped around
cues.zh: 为了让 DNA 井然有序，并调控对遗传密码的访问，它缠绕在

cues.en: these purple proteins, I've labeled them purple here.
cues.zh: 这些紫色的蛋白质上，我在这里把它们标成了紫色。

cues.en: It's packaged up and bundled up.
cues.zh: 它被打包、紧密地捆绑在一起。

cues.en: All of this field of view is a single strand of DNA.
cues.zh: 整个视野里展示的，其实只是一条 DNA 单链。

cues.en: This huge package of DNA is called a chromosome, and we'll come back to chromosomes in a minute.
cues.zh: 这个巨大的 DNA 包裹体被称为染色体，我们稍后还会讲到它。

cues.en: We're pulling out, we're zooming out, out through a nuclear pore, which is sort of
cues.zh: 我们正在拉远镜头，穿过一个核孔往外退，它就像是

cues.en: the gateway to this compartment that holds all the DNA called the nucleus.
cues.zh: 通往存放所有 DNA 的细胞核隔间的门户。

cues.en: All of this field of view is about a semester's worth of biology and I've got seven minutes so we're not going to be able to do that today.
cues.zh: 这整个视野涵盖的内容，差不多相当于一学期的生物课，而我只有七分钟，所以今天讲不完这些。

cues.en: No, I'm being told no.
cues.zh: 不行，有人跟我说不行。

cues.en: This is the way a living cell looks down a light microscope and it's been filmed under time lapse is why you can see it moving.
cues.zh: 这就是活细胞在光学显微镜下的样子，它是用延时摄影拍的，所以你能看到它在活动。

cues.en: The nuclear envelope breaks down.
cues.zh: 核膜破裂了。

cues.en: These sausage shaped things are the chromosomes and we'll focus on them.
cues.zh: 这些香肠状的东西就是染色体，我们重点看它们。

cues.en: They go through this very striking motion that is focused on these little red spots.
cues.zh: 它们会进行这种非常惊人的运动，这种运动集中在这些红色小点上。

cues.en: When the cell feels it's ready to go, it rips apart the chromosome.
cues.zh: 当细胞觉得准备就绪时，它就会把染色体扯开。

cues.en: One set of DNA goes to one side, the other side gets the other set of DNA, identical
cues.zh: 一套DNA移动到一侧，另一侧得到另一套DNA，完全相同的

cues.en: copies of DNA, and then the cell splits down the middle.
cues.zh: DNA拷贝，然后细胞从中间分裂开来。

cues.en: And again, you have billions of cells undergoing this process right now inside of you.
cues.zh: 再说一次，现在你体内就有数十亿个细胞正在经历这个过程。

cues.en: Now we're going to rewind and just focus on the chromosomes and look at its structure
cues.zh: 现在我们倒回去，只关注染色体，看看它的结构

cues.en: and describe it.
cues.zh: 并描述一下。

cues.en: So again, here we are at that equator moment.
cues.zh: 所以，我们又回到了赤道板排列的时刻。

cues.en: Then the chromosomes line up, and if we isolate just one chromosome, we're going to pull it
cues.zh: 染色体排成一行，如果我们单独挑出一个染色体，我们要把它抽

cues.en: out and have a look at its structure.
cues.zh: 出来，看看它的结构。

cues.en: So this is one of the biggest molecular structures that you have, at least as far as we've discovered
cues.zh: 这是人体内最大的分子结构之一，至少就我们目前

cues.en: so far, inside of us.
cues.zh: 所发现的而言。

cues.en: So this is a single chromosome, and you have two strands of DNA in each chromosome.
cues.zh: 这是一条染色体，每条染色体都包含两条DNA链。

cues.en: One is bundled up into one sausage, the other strand is bundled up into the other sausage.
cues.zh: 一条盘绕成一根香肠状，另一条盘绕成另一根香肠状。

cues.en: These things that look like whiskers that are sticking out from either side are the
cues.zh: 这些从两侧伸出来的、像胡须一样的东西，

cues.en: dynamic scaffolding of the cell.
cues.zh: 是细胞的动态支架。

cues.en: They're called microtubules, but mains aren't so important, but we're going to focus on
cues.zh: 它们被称为微管，名称并不太重要，但我们要关注的是

cues.en: this red region.
cues.zh: 这片红色区域。

cues.en: I've labeled it red here, and it's the interface between the dynamic scaffolding and the chromosomes.
cues.zh: 我在这里把它标成了红色，它是动态支架与染色体之间的连接面。

cues.en: It is obviously central to the movement of the chromosomes.
cues.zh: 它显然对染色体的移动起着核心作用。

cues.en: We have no idea, really, as to how it's achieving that movement.
cues.zh: 但实际上，我们根本不知道它是如何实现这种移动的。

cues.en: We've been studying this thing that's called the Kinetochore for over 100 years with
cues.zh: 100多年来，我们一直在对动原体

cues.en: intense study, and we're still just beginning to discover what it's all about.
cues.zh: 进行深入研究，但对它的了解仍处于初级阶段。

cues.en: It is made up of about 200 different types of proteins, thousands of proteins in total.
cues.zh: 它由大约200种不同的蛋白质组成，蛋白质总量达到数千个。

cues.en: It is a signal broadcasting system.
cues.zh: 它是一个信号广播系统。

cues.en: It broadcasts through chemical signals telling the rest of the cell when it's ready, when
cues.zh: 它通过化学信号向细胞的其他部分广播，告知其何时就绪，

cues.en: it feels that everything is aligned and ready to go for the separation of the chromosomes.
cues.zh: 何时确认一切都已对齐，并准备好进行染色体分离。

cues.en: It is able to couple onto the growing and shrinking microtubules.
cues.zh: 它能够结合在不断生长和缩短的微管上。

cues.en: It's transiently, it's involved with the growing of the microtubules, and it's
cues.zh: 它短暂地参与微管的生长，

cues.en: able to transiently couple onto them.
cues.zh: 并且能够短暂地与它们结合。

cues.en: It's also a tension-sensing system.
cues.zh: 它还是一个张力感应系统。

cues.en: It's able to feel when the cell is ready,
cues.zh: 它能够感知细胞何时准备就绪，

cues.en: when the chromosome is correctly positioned.
cues.zh: 染色体何时处于正确的位置。

cues.en: It's turning green here because it feels
cues.zh: 这里正在变成绿色，因为它感知到

cues.en: that everything is just right.
cues.zh: 一切都刚刚好。

cues.en: And you'll see there's this one little last bit
cues.zh: 你会看到还有最后这小小的一小块

cues.en: that's still remaining red,
cues.zh: 依然保持着红色，

cues.en: and it's walked away down the microtubules.
cues.zh: 它正沿着微管走开。

cues.en: That is the signal broadcasting system,
cues.zh: 那是信号广播系统，

cues.en: sending out the stop signal, and it's walked away.
cues.zh: 负责发送停止信号，它已经走开了。

cues.en: I mean, it's that mechanical.
cues.zh: 我是说，它就是这么机械化。

cues.en: It's molecular clockwork.
cues.zh: 这就是分子级的发条装置。

cues.en: This is how you work at the molecular scale.
cues.zh: 在分子尺度上就是这样运作的。

cues.en: So with a little bit of molecular eye candy,
cues.zh: 伴随着这些赏心悦目的分子动画，

cues.en: we've got kinesins, which are the orange ones.
cues.zh: 我们看到了驱动蛋白，也就是橙色的那些。

cues.en: They're little molecular courier molecules walking one way.
cues.zh: 它们就像小小的分子快递员，朝一个方向行走。

cues.en: And here are the dynein.
cues.zh: 而这些是动力蛋白。

cues.en: They're carrying that broadcasting system.
cues.zh: 它们正运送着那个广播系统。

cues.en: And they've got their long legs so they can step around
cues.zh: 它们长着长长的腿，可以跨过

cues.en: obstacles and so on.
cues.zh: 障碍物等等。

cues.en: So again, this is all derived accurately from the science.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这全都严格基于科学依据。

cues.en: The problem is we can't show it to you any other way.
cues.zh: 问题在于，我们无法用其他任何方式展现给你们看。

cues.en: Exploring at the frontier of science,
cues.zh: 探索科学的前沿，

cues.en: at the frontier of human understanding is mind-blowing.
cues.zh: 探索人类认知的边界，是极其震撼人心的。

cues.en: Discovering this stuff is certainly a pleasurable incentive to work in science,
cues.zh: 发现这些东西，固然是投身科研的一种令人愉悦的动力，

cues.en: but most medical researchers, this is just discovering this stuff
cues.zh: 但对大多数医学研究人员而言，发现这些东西

cues.en: is simply steps along the path to the big goals,
cues.zh: 仅仅是迈向宏伟目标的其中几步，

cues.en: which are to eradicate disease,
cues.zh: 那些目标是根除疾病，

cues.en: to eliminate the suffering and the misery that disease causes,
cues.zh: 消除疾病带来的痛苦与苦难，

cues.en: and to lift people out of poverty.
cues.zh: 并带领人们摆脱贫困。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家。
